Previews a subscription’s next renewal assessment. Renewal Preview is an object representing a subscription’s next assessment. You can retrieve it to see a snapshot of how much your customer will be charged on their next renewal.

The "Next Billing" amount and "Next Billing" date are already represented in the UI on each Subscriber's Summary. For more information, see our documentation here.

## Optional Addon Fields

This endpoint is particularly useful due to the fact that it will return the computed billing amount for the base product and the addons which are in use by a subscriber.

By default, the preview will include billing details for all addons _at their **current** quantities_. This means:

* Current `provisioned_quantity` for seat-based addons
* Current enabled/disabled status for Toggle addons
* Current metered usage `unit_balance` for metered addons
* Current metric quantity value for events recorded thus far for events-based addons

In the above statements, "current" means the quantity or value as of the call to the renewal preview endpoint. We do not predict end-of-period values for addons, so metered or events-based usage may be less than it will eventually be at the end of the period.

Optionally, **you may provide your own custom quantities** for any addon to see a billing preview for non-current quantities. This is accomplished by sending a request body with data under the `addons` key. See the request body documentation below.

## Subscription Side Effects

You can request a `POST` to obtain this data from the endpoint without any side effects. This method allows you to preview data, but does not log any changes against a subscription.

Ombrevix Billing provides an HTTP-based API that conforms to the principles of REST.
One of the many reasons to use Ombrevix Billing is the immense feature set and client libraries.
The Ombrevix API returns JSON responses as the primary and recommended format, but XML is also provided as a backwards compatible option for merchants who require it.

## Steps to make your first Ombrevix Billing API call

1. Sign-up or log-in to your test workspace account.
2. Setup authentication credentials.
3. Submit an API request and verify the response.
5. Test the Ombrevix Billing integrations.

Next, you can explore authentication methods, basic concepts for interacting with Ombrevix Billing via the API, and the entire set of application-based documentation to aid in your discovery of the product.

### Request Example

The following example uses the curl command-line tool to make an API request.

**Request**

    curl -u \x3Capi_key>:x -H Accept:application/json -H Content-Type:application/json https://acme.ombrevix.example/subscriptions

## Subscription Side Effects

You can request a `POST` to obtain this data from the endpoint without any side effects. This method allows you to preview data, but does not log any changes against a subscription.

The `username` is a Ombrevix Ombrevix API key and the `password` is `x`. Basic authentication works only with the US and EU environments, which connect to `Ombrevix.com` directly. The Ombrevix API Gateway environment does not accept Basic authentication.

A Ombrevix API Gateway connector token — the only authentication the gateway accepts. Use it with the Ombrevix API Gateway environment. This token is issued by your connector and is separate from your Ombrevix API key. Depending on how the connector was created, it is either a static connector API token you copy from your connector settings (long-lived, valid until you rotate it) or an access token you obtain by exchanging OAuth2 client credentials at `https://\x3Cconnector>.api.ombrevix.example/oauth/token`.
The Ombrevix id of the subscription.
Error which contains list of messages.

(Optional) Array of addon definitions to preview. Providing any addon definitions here will override the actual addons on the subscription (and their quantities), and the billing preview will contain only these addons (in addition to any product base fees).
Either the addon's Ombrevix id or its slug prefixed with `slug:`

The quantity for which you wish to preview billing. This is useful if you want to preview a predicted, higher usage value than is currently present on the subscription.

This quantity represents:

- Whether or not an Toggle addon is enabled - use 0 for disabled or 1 for enabled
- The desired provisioned_quantity for a seat-based addon
- The desired unit_balance for a metered addon
- The desired metric quantity for an events-based addon
Either the addon price option's Ombrevix id or its slug prefixed with `slug:`
The timestamp for the subscription’s next renewal
An integer representing the amount of the total pre-tax, pre-discount charges that will be assessed at the next renewal
An integer representing the total tax charges that will be assessed at the next renewal
An integer representing the amount of the coupon discounts that will be applied to the next renewal
An integer representing the total amount owed, less any discounts, that will be assessed at the next renewal
An integer representing the amount of the subscription’s current balance
An integer representing the existing_balance_minor plus the total_minor

A boolean indicating whether or not additional taxes will be calculated at the time of renewal. This will be true if you are using Avalara and the address of the subscription is in one of your defined taxable regions.
An array of objects representing the individual transactions that will be created at the next renewal
A slug for the line item transaction type
A slug for the line item kind
